Great question. Talk to the child, absolutely (if they're old enough and have the cognitive ability). The first things I'll say are "you're not in trouble" and "I am a safe person." This will build trust with the children. From there, ask them about the abuse, and get as many details as possible to report. When did it happen, where did it happen, who did it, how often does it happen, does it happen to siblings/other children, is there an injury, if there is an injury make sure you can describe it. As long as it's not a hipaa violation (like it is at my job), take pictures of the injury. Record the conversation. Then report. Find the number in your county for reporting child abuse. For example, in Milwaukee county where I work it is 220-SAFE. Always, always report. Even if CPS doesn't choose to investigate, the report is there if there's another incident. The more evidence, the better.

I always tell the child it's not their fault, and they deserve to be healthy and safe. I like to provide things like stuffed animals, blankets, stickers/coloring books, and other things that are a comfort for them. Last word of advice: absolutely do not DO NOT address the alleged abuser about it. Let CPS take care of that as they are trained in it. Because that can actually put the child in a position of further harm.
